material.description: ci-status 3ea3cf0: run 38753273421. Windows build, spike and gate job fails (exit 1 from oscraft-gate.exe); ubuntu and macos pass; the ubuntu log shows the same 19 failures ('gate: 108 checks, 19 failed'). Causes: (a) two checks, editor-terrain-tiles and editor-abilities, call string.find inside mod Lua. HEAD mod-host compile() whitelists only error, assert, type, tostring, tonumber, select, pairs, ipairs, next, so global string is nil; fix in rust/gate/src/claimed_checks.rs lines 385, 388, 408 by using method form (tostring(x):find(s, 1, true)) which needs no global. (b) 17 checks report 'missing API' because the sim does not expose the read the gate probes (ranged-miss-chance, elevation-sight, channel-interrupt, worker-saturation, geyser-extraction, opening-resources, base-resource-nodes, supply-cap, supply-providers, supply-reservation, rally-point, tech-prerequisites, research-queue, research-applies-all, damage-type-size, cloak-detection) and upgrade-stacking reports effect-unsupported. Several of these names are public on HEAD per recent commits (e.g. rally_point 3ea3cf0, supply_providers af1cd36), so the gate's API probe and HEAD disagree; reconcile the probe with HEAD first. Working tree is not used for this fix: rust/crates/mod-host/src/lib.rs in the working tree is an older stripped copy of HEAD and must not be committed (see publish-blocked-dirty-tree).

material.acceptance_criteria: Client errors are appended to a server-owned log file in the data directory that survives a restart, with a size cap that rotates the file.
material.description: rust/crates/server/src/relay.rs:35-47 writes client errors with println! only, so nothing persists across a restart or is owned by the server as a log file. The rate-limit table is a process-wide static (relay.rs:24-27) that restarts empty.
material.resolution: Client errors append to a server-owned log, rotated at 1 MiB, with stdout unchanged. The rate-limit bucket is restored from the log tail on first request after start, so a restart does not reset it. Add a real cost reduction under overrun (for example skip a named set of non-essential per-tick sim systems or mod ticks while shedding, restored on recovery) and strengthen the generous-budget CI check so it posts orders and asserts zero tick-shed lines under a loose budget.

material.acceptance_criteria: A committed baseline file records p50, p90 and p99 for a fixed scenario, and a CI step fails when a fresh run's p99 exceeds the baseline by more than a stated margin.
material.description: rust/crates/server/src/budget.rs prints tick-time p50, p90, p99 and max every 80 ticks. The tick-budget job in .github/workflows/ci.yml checks only the line format and runs with a 1 us budget or a 20 ms budget. material.acceptance_criteria: After a .star edit adds a unit kind, the running server without restart serves it in GET /catalog and a mod can spawn it, within 5 seconds of the image rebuild.
material.description: oscraftd reads --data once in Room::new (rust/crates/server/src/room.rs, sim::load_file) and mods.rs reads the image once at startup. The hot path (mod-host reload) covers only the Lua mod file. A unit or behaviour compiled from data/*.star is therefore absent from the running server until restart, and no CI job checks a data edit reaching the served catalog.
material.resolution: A .star edit reaches the running server without a restart: a poll thread rebuilds the data image, validates it, and the tick swaps it in at a boundary, logging ev=data_reloaded. A failed rebuild logs ev=data_reload_failed and keeps the live image. Limits: the swap resets the match (follow-up gap-data-reload-keeps-match-state); the mod host keeps the startup image (follow-up gap-mod-host-follows-data-reload); a map size change is refused and needs a restart.
material.subject: A data-only .star change that adds a unit or behaviour needs a server restart

material.acceptance_criteria: One API definition (the WIT file) drives both targets: every WIT export has a wasip1 command, and a generated dispatch file is checked in CI so that adding an export without its wasip1 counterpart fails the build.

material.acceptance_criteria: a CI run spawns a unit through a mod, reloads the data, and the mod's handle still orders the same unit.
material.description: The data swap clears the room's handle map, so a mod's handles stop resolving after a reload even though the carried units keep their indices. Remap handles to the carried indices instead of clearing them.
material.resolution: A mod's handle keeps working across a data reload: a unit removed by the new map is placed back at its original index with spawn_at, so the handle still orders it. CI checks the unit moves and no unmapped refusal is logged. Gaps filed: a handle is kept when any unit is alive at the index even if its kind changed; a handle whose kind is absent from the new catalog is dropped silently.

material.acceptance_criteria: parseGlb rejects a POSITION accessor whose type is not VEC3, or readAccessor returns the vertex count; a live witness on a non-VEC3 POSITION fixture shows the error.
material.description: js/client/glb.js:73-74 and :76. parseGlb derives the index count from positions.length / 3, while readAccessor (line 36) owns the element width from accessor.type. The 3 is a second copy of the VEC3 fact, so a non-VEC3 POSITION accessor is not rejected at the accessor boundary and yields a wrong index count.

material.acceptance_criteria: Row net-e2e-two-peers unblocked by an explicit ownership decision on js/host/frame.js and js/client/frame.js, and a pinned relay dependency version.
material.description: Facts at remote main 7db475cd605b81f6a0b73b9bc327b7050b5048da: (1) js/host/frame.js encodeState emits tick/units/hash only, no positions; js/client/frame.js decodeState expects u32 id, f32 x, f32 z, u8 player per unit. (2) js/host/frame.js decodeFrame reads order as int32 x,y; js/client/frame.js encodeOrderMove writes f32 x,z. (3) js/wire/frame.js (the intended replacement, other lane) is not imported by either side. (4) The guest exposes unit-position <id> -> 'ok unit-position x y' and order <unit> x y (rust/crates/wasip1/src/lib.rs), so positions are obtainable host-side. (5) play.html needs pkg/web.js and map.bin in the served dir; no CI job builds js/client/pkg. (6) js/host/package.json has no WebSocket server dependency for a local relay. Fixing (1) and (2) requires editing js/host/frame.js and js/client/frame.js, which are outside this row's ownership list. Options for the orchestrator: widen ownership to those two codec files, or assign the codec to js/wire lane first.

material.description: blocked_by: gap-mod-unit-id-mapping. Remote main facts (ref=main, tip cb054d35). (1) mod-host lib.rs ~707-716: game.cmd_spawn pushes Cmd::Spawn{index: catalog index, x, y} with no unit id; the Lua call returns nothing, so the mod never learns an id. (2) mod-host lib.rs ~301-316: host spawn_unit spawns directly into the mod world and discards Sim::spawn's Option<usize> (sim/src/arrays.rs:521); it does not queue Cmd::Spawn. (3) mod-host lib.rs ~1045-1046 apply_commands spawns into the mod world and discards the index; it only runs for commands queued by systems (tick order: run_systems, apply_commands, fire_timers, run_on_tick), so on_tick cmd_spawn commands are never applied to the mod world and go straight to the room via take_commands (lib.rs ~1171, mods.rs ~94). (4) room.rs ~247-248 discards sim.spawn's index. Consequence: no mod-world index exists at queue time on the queued path, and a mod that spawns via cmd_spawn has no id to order. The decided carry-the-index design needs another id source (e.g. a mod-side monotonic handle returned by cmd_spawn, keyed in the room map). That is a design change beyond the one-field scope; orchestrator decision needed.

material.description: blocked_by: gap-data-reload-keeps-match-state. Facts (remote main a69d4b3c): room.rs step() swaps the staged Sim (~237-241) with no carry. Per-unit carry needs the unit type index: Sim.type_of is pub(crate) with no pub accessor in sim/src/arrays.rs, so kind cannot be mapped by name into the new catalog. hp is settable only via private fields; spawn_for resets hp to full. Sim::load_state restores hp, ids and positions but copies the OLD terrain flags/tiles and keeps the new catalog, so using it would silently drop map.star terrain edits. Needed: a read-only pub unit_type(i) -> Option<u32> and a pub hp setter in sim, outside this lane. A new Ev for match_carried needs log.rs (other lane); fallback is Ev::DataReloaded with carried=/dropped= fields.

material.description:
blocked_by: gap-mod-effects-reach-served-room (orient, remote main 60912eaa440bb47075a65a65ff79a1f085c66d3e)
fact: the mod effects cannot reach the served room through the allowed surface.
1. ModHost (rust/crates/mod-host/src/lib.rs blob a4c8d1e3) keeps its command queue private: `cmds: Cmds = Rc<RefCell<Vec<Cmd>>>` with enum Cmd {Spawn,Order,Damage,Buff}; not pub, not reachable from server.
2. spawn_unit in bind_host writes the mod's private world immediately (no queue), so there is no pending list to read.
3. The only public door to the mod world is ModHost::sim() -> RefMut<Sim>. Sim exposes no public unit-kind accessor (kind is pub(crate), sim/src/arrays.rs), so a spawn cannot be replayed into the room with spawn_for(player, kind, x, y) from outside the sim crate.
4. ModLink (rust/crates/server/src/mods.rs blob f228fd4d) publishes only version and tick; room.rs (blob 0b567732) Clock owns a separate Sim with no hook for foreign effects.
Fixing it needs a mod-host change exposing pending commands or unit kind (outside this row's ownership), or a sim accessor (forbidden by the row). Neither was done; nothing pushed.

material.description: blocked_by gap-mod-effects-reach-served-room. Remote main 5de402ac: the only call site that hands a room to the ticker is server/src/lib.rs run() (spawn_ticker(Arc::clone(room), tick_budget), line 69) and the ModLink is created there (line 60). material.acceptance_criteria: mod-host Cmd::Spawn carries the mod-world unit index or reports it on spawn; room.rs fills a mod-to-room map at spawn and refuses+logs unmapped order/damage/buff ids; CI mod-reach job proves spawn-then-order moves the served unit.
material.description: Remote main cb054d35. room.rs apply_mod_commands (lines 243-269) receives mod_host::Cmd, and Cmd::Spawn { index, x, y } (mod-host/src/lib.rs:67) carries the catalog index only, not the mod-world unit id. sim.spawn returns Option<usize> (sim/src/arrays.rs:521), discarded at room.rs:248. mod-host cmd_spawn (lib.rs:709-717) pushes the same variant; mod-host apply_commands (lib.rs:1040) drains the mod's own queue via mem::take, and take_commands (lib.rs:1171) drains on_tick/timer commands, so the mod world and the room never apply the same spawn list. Without the mod-side index in the command, the room cannot key the map. Fix needs Cmd::Spawn to carry the mod world index (or mod-host to report the allocated index), which is mod-host scope and out of this row's ownership. Row gap-mod-unit-id-mapping stays pending with blocked_by this id.

material.description: Witness run for gap-moba-winner-readout-blocker-gm-orch-1-15 (session gm-orch-1-22). Served room: oscraftd --data scenarios/moba --mod <disposable fog-off mod> --ticks 100000000 (binary rust/target/debug/oscraftd built 22:11, HEAD e03ee19). The base is the side-1 unit with the highest hp, id 1 (spawned first in map.osd; catalog declaration index 2 is 'base', but GET /state records carry a sim kind, not the catalog index, so kind 2 does not appear). Mod: game.cmd_set_fog(false) once, then every owner-0 unit game.cmd_attack on the side-1 unit with the most hp. Measured: the base hp fell 98304000 -> 51642368 by tick 1702 and was 51380224 at tick 2600 and 49283072 at tick 2776 (side-1 base hp at 2776 on the last state read: 51380224 for id 1; id 19 at 49283072 is a side-1 unit). winner stayed -1 through tick 2776. Side-0 attackers (ids 0,4,6,8,14,16,18,20-23) sat at x 181k-450k while the base is at x ~2.3M, so attack orders are accepted (applied=21 per tick) but do not close distance. Without fog off, the orders were refused because the base was unseen (mod-host test cmd_attack_on_an_unseen_target_is_refused_by_the_sim). Not witnessed: no RESULT line; the row stays pending. Next probe: measure per-attacker distance to the target across ticks and whether units reach weapon range; a longer tick bound (the run took about 4.5 minutes for 2800 ticks at tick-budget-us 20000).

material.description: The sim declares a winner through declare_winner (rust/crates/sim/src/triggers.rs, Sim::winner()), and the gate prints win trigger ok from its own scenario. The served /state and the server log do not report the winner for a running room, so the moba job cannot print moba match ok winner=<side> ticks=<n> without reading it. scenarios/moba now tags bases with building and declares the winner on base loss (win_on_base_loss); the match check is left out until the winner is readable.

material.description: blocked_by: gap-tick-overrun-action. Live evidence (ELIMINATE, receipts/gap-tick-overrun-action/01-orient.md): (1) shedding already exists (budget.rs:16-22, room.rs step) and only defers order drains; (2) implementing the owner's paths cadence (run paths every SHED_PATHS_EVERY=4 ticks while shedding, units every tick) in tick.rs/room.rs/budget.rs and running oscraftd --ci room: at budget 1us shed engages but overruns still climb (4388/4400 ticks); at budget 22us no shed ever engages and overruns are sporadic OS noise (0-2 per 1000 ticks, 14 in 7345); the paths system is ~2-4us of a ~20us ci tick, so shed ticks are barely cheaper than full ticks. (3) Structural: a paths tick is a full-cost tick, so under any budget where full cost > budget the overrun counter keeps rising at 1/N; and the streak reset on any under-budget shed tick flaps shedding off. The acceptance 'overrun count stops increasing' is not reachable by a bounded paths cadence. Edits reverted to HEAD e6d39a16; nothing pushed. Needed owner decision: change the acceptance to a rate bound, add hysteresis, or shed a heavier pass (e.g. Units or Vision) in a loaded catalog.

material.description: blocked_by: gap-tick-cost-reduction-under-overrun. The 1 us tight run measures sim.tick() at about 2 us per tick on CI (run 38898909117, 2059 tick-overrun lines). Named non-sim work in room.rs step (drain, Instant reads, histogram, println) is not a cost the sim pays and cannot bring cost_us under 1 us. So the overrun counter keeps incrementing every tick under the tight run; the stop-climbing acceptance is unreachable without redefining overrun, which would be gaming the counter. Receipt: .gm/receipts/gap-tick-cost-reduction-under-overrun/01-orient.md. Needs an owner decision: (a) a bound stated on shed ticks only with a budget above the measured sim floor, or (b) change the acceptance to the loose-budget half, which is achievable.

material.description: Reproduced with a local mirror (http://127.0.0.1:8899) and wireweave's EphemeralRelay on ws://127.0.0.1:43199: guest published an offer (ts 1792692242978), host joined afterwards, and the host's __ciDebug (?ci=1) shows two peer connections both ice="new", conn="new", remoteMdns=0 — peers created from presence, but no SDP ever applied and no answer published. The offer is one-shot: once missed, neither side re-offers, so both sit at 'peers 0 (local)' indefinitely. data.js:_handleSignal answers offers via doAnswer, but nothing re-sends an offer when the peer never answers.

material.description: Surface: js/client/feedback.js. Principle: Make Illegal States Unrepresentable (ILLEGAL). The armed state can be set with no position: onEvent 'targetArm' sets armed.on=true (feedback.js:89-94) while the only writer of armed.client is the pointermove listener (feedback.js:108). drawTargeting hides both reticle and area when `!armed.on || !armed.client` (feedback.js:161). The producer arm() in scenarios/moba/controls.lua:201 sends slot, item, radius and targetKind, and no pointer position. Symptom: a targeted or ground-target cast armed before any pointer movement since page load shows no reticle and no area ring. Witness: codesearch literal 'armed.client' (feedback.js:108,161,167,172) and 'targetArm' (controls.lua:201). Fix direction, not applied: carry the pointer position in the arm event, or fall back to the last known screen position.
material.resolution: resolved

material.acceptance_criteria: A pointercancel clears press and box, and the overlay is hidden. onDown clears any leftover box before a new press. After a touch drag that the browser cancels, no selection rectangle remains on screen.
material.description: moba_input.js registers only pointerdown, pointermove and pointerup (moba_input.js:57-59). No pointercancel handler exists under js/client, and no touch-action rule is set. When the browser takes a touch as a pan, it fires pointercancel and no pointerup, so onUp (moba_input.js:50-54) never clears press or box. onDown (moba_input.js:38-42) does not clear box either, and onMove (moba_input.js:44-48) keeps updating box from pointer moves that carry no button. Symptom: after a one-finger drag on the map, a green selection rectangle stays on screen and follows the pointer until the next pointerup. This affects phone layouts, which the project targets.
material.subject: A cancelled press leaves the drag box on screen until the next tap
material.witness: Live page (verify-illegal-trav-input-client-2): after pointerdown and an 80px drag, pointercancel now sets overlay display none (drag:block | cancel:none | moveNoButton:none | repress:none); before the fix the overlay stayed block at 80px then 150px.

material.acceptance_criteria: OWN_FILL and NEUTRAL_FILL (ui_minimap.js:10-11) reach at least 3:1 against each other, or a non-colour cue (outline or ring) marks own units, so own and neutral units are distinguishable without relying on size.
material.description: Principle DADA_CRAP (Contrast). OWN_FILL #ffffff (js/client/ui_minimap.js:11) and NEUTRAL_FILL #c2c8ce (ui_minimap.js:10) have a WCAG relative-luminance contrast of 1.69:1, below the 3:1 non-text threshold (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11). The two are told apart mainly by size: own creeps draw at 5 px through sizeFor (ui_minimap.js:22-24, own || hero), neutral creeps at 3 px. Witness: codesearch dispatch 1792858709793-5767-ab6825f62c68d61c.

notes.note: Triage refute (principle-only, no observable failure). The 1.69:1 figure compares OWN_FILL #ffffff with NEUTRAL_FILL #c2c8ce (ui_minimap.js:10-11) against each other; WCAG 1.4.11 measures each graphic against its adjacent background, and both pass on BACKGROUND #1a2129 (ui_minimap.js:17): own 16.24:1, neutral 9.62:1 (WCAG relative luminance, computed in gm_codemode). The two dots also differ by size (own 5 px via sizeFor :22-24, neutral 3 px via SIZE.creep :8), so neither is identified by colour alone. No player-visible failure is shown. Read: ui_minimap.js 8-24 dispatch 1792859769608-6581-cef0c3d1d16a4a (session verify-DADA_CRAP-trav-minimap-camera-2).

material.resolution: Stale: the premise (1.69:1 between own and neutral fills is a WCAG non-text failure) is refuted; both fills pass 3:1 against the background, and the pair differs by size.

material.acceptance_criteria: A window blur releases the modifiers the pack holds (a forwarded up per held modifier, or a blur action). A ground press after refocus carries shift=false unless shift is physically down.
material.description: play.js:1262 handles window blur by clearing keysDown only. It sends no key release for held modifiers. The pack takes shift, ctrl and alt only from key events (controls.lua:427-428), and each ground press copies shift from that state (controls.lua:475). A shift keydown followed by focus loss (alt-tab) never delivers its keyup to the page, so s.held.shift stays true until another key event arrives. The next right-click then passes shift as the queued flag (controls.lua:490, order_selected at controls.lua:231). Symptom: after returning to the game, a plain right-click queues the move instead of replacing the order.
material.subject: Modifier keys stay held in the pack after the window loses focus
material.witness: Live page (verify-illegal-trav-input-client-3), pack dispatch spy: keydown Shift then window blur. Before the fix the blur sent no key event after shift down (dispatch 1792859828185-6599-dc1cafad6b690914). After the fix it sent key shift up with shift false (dispatch 1792859865102-6619-466d4037f6a6d6b8).

material.acceptance_criteria: After any sequence of orbit deltas, the pitch stays in the documented range and eyeOf(cam)[1] >= 0. Every screen corner used by viewRect maps to a finite ground point.
material.description: render3d.js:5 defines PITCH_LIMIT = PI/2 - 0.01, and orbitCamera at render3d.js:196 clamps pitch to [-PITCH_LIMIT, PITCH_LIMIT], so the lower bound is negative. render3d.js:120 documents pitch as 'above the ground plane', and eyeOf (render3d.js:121-127) puts the eye at target.y + distance*sin(pitch), so a negative pitch puts the eye under the ground. Input reaches it from play.js:1227 (pointermove, button 2 held or shift down, calls renderer3d.orbit) through render3d.js:555. The default pitch is 0.9 rad and the drag rate is 0.005 rad/px (render3d.js:194), so about 180 px of upward right-drag reaches pitch 0 and more reaches the underside. Symptom: the view flips under the map, and screenToWorld (play.js:1107-1125), which feeds the viewport rectangle (moba_input.js:26-41) and every ground click, then casts rays away from the ground.
material.subject: Right-drag orbit can take the camera pitch below the ground plane
material.witness: Re-checked on origin/main (ci-status 194e15a3: 6/6 success, run 40112738370). render3d.js:5 PITCH_LIMIT = PI/2-0.01 and :7 PITCH_MIN = PI/6+0.01; orbitCamera (render3d.js:198) clamps pitch to [PITCH_MIN, PITCH_LIMIT], so the lower bound is positive and eye height stays above the ground. Witness dispatch 1792860044680-6698-40c935ea58cc7143 from its own session. Row resolved on the fix sha 194e15a3, which is an ancestor of origin/main.

material.acceptance_criteria: A right press that play.js treats as an orbit issues no order on release. The camera-drag threshold and the pack's click threshold come from one value, or the pack ignores right releases that followed a moved drag.
material.description: play.js:57 sets DRAG_SLOP_PX = 4, and play.js:1223 marks a right-button drag as moved after 4 px. That drag orbits the camera (play.js:1227). play.js:1236 forwards every pointer up to the pack, whatever the drag state. The pack decides 'moved' in ground tiles: controls.lua:481 compares the press and release points with CFG.dragSlop, which is 0.25 (controls.lua:37, moba_ui.json:62). When the release is not moved, controls.lua:482-490 calls order_selected for a right click. The screen centre stays fixed while the view yaws, and the ground under other pixels moves about r*dyaw, so a 4-10 px orbit near the centre reads as a click. Symptom: nudging the camera with the right button walks the selected units to the release point.
material.subject: A short right-drag that orbits the camera also issues a move order on release
material.witness: Re-checked on origin/main (ci-status eec4a2ce: 6/6 success, run 40112898029). play.js:1234-1237 drops the pointerup forward to the pack when the right drag moved (DRAG_SLOP_PX=4, play.js:57), so the pack takes no order for a moved release. Witness dispatch 1792860191938-6776-e56cae65407e6aa3 from its own session. Row resolved on the fix sha eec4a2ce, an ancestor of origin/main.

material.acceptance_criteria: Pitch has a lower bound of 0 (or a small positive minimum) so the eye stays above the ground, and the clamp matches the documented contract.
material.description: render3d.js:120 documents eyeOf as pitch above the ground plane, and nearOf (render3d.js:134-137) assumes the nearest floor is in front of the eye. orbitCamera (render3d.js:196) clamps pitch to [-PITCH_LIMIT, PITCH_LIMIT], with PITCH_LIMIT = PI/2 - 0.01 (render3d.js:5). An upward shift or right-button drag (play.js:1227 orbit) takes pitch below 0, where eye height distance*sin(pitch) is below the target.

material.acceptance_criteria: After a hero dies, its expanded team-strip row reads state dead with a zero or blank hp, not the pre-death value, on the next refresh.
material.description: Symptom: an expanded team-strip row for a dead hero shows the last hp read while alive, under state dead. Cause: scenarios/moba/panels.lua:194 stores hp only in the alive branch; the dead branch (panels.lua:196) sets state without clearing hp. game.units() lists living units only (rust/crates/mod-host/src/piccolo_host.rs:2215), so the dead branch always runs. Shown at panels.lua:318. Contract broken: HEROES[p].hp must hold the hero's current hp. Working-tree line numbers at trav-hud-lua-L2 walk; panels.lua grew 14 lines below line 505 during the walk.

material.description: Fact: createMinimap (js/client/ui_minimap.js:38-197) adds pointerdown and pointermove listeners to its canvas (js/client/ui_minimap.js:186, 191) and a pointerup listener to window (js/client/ui_minimap.js:194). Callers: js/client/hmr.js:47, js/client/play.js:2360, js/client/play.js:2561. Each hot reload stacks one more set of three listeners and the earlier closures keep running. Symptom: a press on the minimap calls centre() once per stacked set, and the listener count grows by three per reload.

material.acceptance_criteria: With gold below a recipe item's net price its buy button is disabled and its price tone is bad; at or above the net price it is enabled and the purchase is accepted.
material.description: Symptom: a recipe item with gold below its net price shows a gold-toned price and an enabled buy button; the purchase is then refused. Cause: scenarios/moba/panels.lua:363 sets afford true for every item with components (#def.components > 0 or ...), skipping the gold check; the tone at panels.lua:366 and the buy disable at panels.lua:372 follow it. The engine prices at def.cost minus held components and refuses below that (scenarios/moba/store.lua:108-110, reason cannot-afford). Contract broken: the shop affordability predicate must equal the purchase precondition.
material.subject: Shop enables buy on recipe items the player cannot pay for
material.witness: Recipe buy now uses the net price. Codesearch (session verify-dbc-trav-hud-lua-L2-2, dispatch 1792863244838-5123-4b1f42b18caa9bc7): the afford line is now gold >= price with price = net_price(hero, i, def) at panels.lua:358-359; net_price (line 326) mirrors store.lua acquire (cost less held components, recursive claim). CI green on head 4b24d0bc. Witness is code-level; the live shop check was not run.
material.witness_plan: Live shop check: set gold just below a recipe's net price with no components held, read the card's buy disabled state, press it and confirm the cannot-afford refusal; repeat at the net price.

material.acceptance_criteria: After pointerdown followed by pointercancel, a later pointermove on the canvas does not call centre(); the sequence is covered by a test or live check.
material.description: Fact: js/client/ui_minimap.js:187 sets pressed on pointerdown, and only the window pointerup listener clears it (ui_minimap.js:194). The file has no pointercancel listener (codesearch over js/: 0 hits, dispatch 1792858548708-4738-3ef1ddb916bdf4d3), and the #minimap rule in js/client/play.html:149 sets no touch-action. When the browser cancels a press (pointercancel, not pointerup), pressed stays true, and the next pointermove on the canvas calls centreAt (ui_minimap.js:191-192), moving the camera with no button held. Counterexample: pointerdown on the canvas, pointercancel, then pointermove on the canvas, which calls centre() where it should not. Reproduces on a touch-capable screen that also has a mouse. Distinct from the press-leaves-canvas row OWNERSHIP-trav-minimap-camera-1 and the moba_input.js row illegal-trav-input-client-2.

material.acceptance_criteria: ui_minimap.js calls setPointerCapture on pointerdown and releases it on pointerup, so a mouse press dragged past the canvas edge keeps moving the camera.
material.description: js/client/ui_minimap.js:186-193. pointerdown sets pressed and centres the camera; pointermove on the canvas centres only while pressed. The file never calls setPointerCapture (editor.js:289, play.js:1216 and replay.js:255 do). With a mouse, pointermove stops reaching the canvas once the pointer leaves it, so the camera freezes at the edge until the pointer re-enters. clamp01 at ui_minimap.js:180-181 handles out-of-box coordinates, which only arrive with capture. Touch is implicitly captured by the browser, so the defect is mouse-only. Witness: codesearch dispatches 1792858291900-4014-44d9352df8dea157 (capture sites) and 1792858346256-4193-eb35f0fc5aa17c85 (listener lines).

Target https://lanmower.github.io/oscraft/js/client/play.html?host=1 (live version.json sha 11edb063; play.js line numbers match origin 4b24d0b, 3191 lines). 1280x720, cache disabled, real relay (no relay param), fresh isolated tab each load, CDP Debugger logpoints (breakpoint conditions that record performance.now and return false; no code change).
Load | main await | build3d total | splat await | unitFitsReady await | status at 15 s | relay (console)
C1 | 10380 | 10377 | 10214 | 0 | loading world assets | not captured
C2 | 10563 | 10558 | 10159 | 237 | loading world assets | wss://relay.damus.io/ 503
C3 | 12746 | 12742 | 12583 | 0 | loading world assets | wss://relay.damus.io/ 503
C4 | 24228 | 24223 | 24059 | 0 | loading world assets | no relay error logged
C5 | 13171 | 13167 | 13013 | 0 | loading world assets | no relay error logged
All loads: status read "joined" by the ~70 s sample. The 15 s stall message was not sampled; splat exceeded 15 s only in C4 (24.1 s). material.acceptance_criteria: Within every group, the gap between siblings is smaller than the gap between separate groups: the .w-box.row item gap is below the .w-root panel gap, and the .w-panel>h4 title-to-first-child gap is no larger than the gap between that panel's sibling children. Static: the gap and margin values at widgets.js:26-31 and 46 satisfy that order.
material.description: Surface: js/client/widgets.js (STYLE block; buildNode panel branch). Principle: Gestalt proximity (Wertheimer, Koffka, Köhler). Two spacing values place group-internal gaps above the gap between separate groups. (a) .w-box.row sets gap:6px (widgets.js:31) between sibling items of one row, while .w-root sets gap:4px between sibling panels (widgets.js:26), so two buttons in one row sit farther apart than two stacked panels. (b) buildNode appends the h4 title as the first child of section.w-panel (widgets.js:141-142). .w-panel has a flex gap of 4px (widgets.js:28) and .w-panel>h4 has margin-bottom 4px (widgets.js:29), so the title sits 8px above its first child while the panel's own children sit 4px apart. Panels stay closed by their 1px border, so this weakens grouping rather than clipping anything. Surface: js/client/hud.js asserts no cause; this row is a CSS finding in widgets.js.
material.subject: Panel spacing inverts the proximity hierarchy: row items sit farther apart than separate panels, and a panel title floats away from its content
material.witness: Live stylesheet rules on Pages: .w-root gap 6px, .w-box.row gap 4px, .w-panel gap 4px, .w-panel>h4 margin-bottom 0px. Row item gap 4 < root gap 6; title-to-child 0+4 is not above sibling gap 4. Rendered-panel computed values not reachable after reload (no widget panels rendered). Fix e2bdb948 on origin tip. CI on tip 7f68d3bcc7c7356b1291ccec7eda0b23ad2a89f2 green (ci-status 6/6 success, run 40128978828).

material.acceptance_criteria: Each expanded team-strip hero row shows whole hp equal to the select panel's health number for the same hero at the same tick.
material.description: Symptom: the expanded team strip prints each hero's hp as a Q16.16 integer (550 hp reads as 36044800) while the select and HUD panels show whole hp. Cause: scenarios/moba/panels.lua:318 prints h.hp unscaled; h.hp is unit_hp stored at panels.lua:194 and is Q16.16 (config.FIX = 65536, scenarios/moba/shared/config.lua:3). The same module divides by config.FIX at panels.lua:230 and :483. Rivals: unit_hp returns whole hp (rejected: mods/bot_probe.lua:30 and :37 divide unit_hp by 65536); the select and HUD sites are wrong (rejected: they divide by FIX). Representation leaks past the hp accessor into the team strip.

material.acceptance_criteria: Skill-up with no hero selected calls refuse(who, 'noHero'), the same as the cast and item keys, and the player sees 'select a hero first'.
material.description: scenarios/moba/controls.lua:369-372 skill_up returns silently when hero_selected is nil. The same no-hero case refuses with the 'noHero' text elsewhere: cast_key at :317, item_key at :336, resolve_armed at :353. scenarios/moba/moba_ui.json:176 supplies the text 'select a hero first'. The HUD path on_action('skill_up') (:~426) reaches the same silent return. Symptom: a player who presses the skill-up key with a non-hero selection sees nothing happen, while the cast key shows the reason. Visibility of system status (Nielsen heuristic 1) is violated for this one key. The sim-side refusal (no skill point) is not covered here: cmd_skill_up sends no answer to the mod.

notes.note: Citation fix: the HUD path on_action('skill_up') is scenarios/moba/controls.lua:555 (calls skill_up at :555), not ~426. Confirmed the other cites: :317, :336, :353 refuse noHero; :369 skill_up silent; moba_ui.json:176.

material.acceptance_criteria: A key event without a ground point casts nothing at a made-up point: the mod refuses it with a reason, or the page omits world and the mod uses the hero position for self-centred casts.
material.description: js/client/play.js:270 sets the key's ground point to null while pointer is null (no pointermove since load), then play.js:278 sends world {x:0,z:0}. scenarios/moba/controls.lua:436 reads a.world.x and a.world.z without a sentinel check, and cast_key (:315) passes that point to cast_now at :330 for an ability with no target type. The sentinel parses as a valid point, so an ability with no cast_range is cast at (0,0), and one with a cast_range is refused as 'range' at :325 with the cursor position not the cause. Symptom: a keyboard-first player who has not moved the mouse since page load gets an AoE at the map corner or a misleading out-of-range refusal. Narrow: applies only until the first pointermove.

notes.note: Citation fix: the range refusal in cast_key is scenarios/moba/controls.lua:329 (out_of_range then refuse 'range'), not :325. The other cites hold: :315 cast_key, :330 cast_now, :436 a.world read; js/client/play.js:270 and :278.

material.acceptance_criteria: After a shift-queued unit dies, QUEUE holds no entry for its id on the next tick, and on_tick returns at the next(QUEUE) check when no living unit has a queue.
material.description: scenarios/moba/controls.lua:218 declares QUEUE; :248-250 append a queued order per unit; the only deletes are :252 (non-queued issue), :262 (stop), :270 (hold) and :602 (empty queue of a living unit). on_tick (:587-605) skips a unit with game.alive(id) false at :600 and never removes its entry. After one shift-queued unit dies, next(QUEUE) (:587) is never nil again, so every tick rebuilds and insertion-sorts every leaked id (:590-597). Symptom: per-tick Lua cost and table size grow with each queued unit killed in a match. Fix: drop QUEUE[id] for a dead unit in on_tick, or clear it from the death path.

notes.note: Published controls.lua 3292a7ca (on_tick drops a dead unit's QUEUE entry). Witness blocked: no Lua runtime in this sandbox for a standalone run and no live match: Live check (browser dispatch 1792862772886-5303-5a481f4722e0f263, session verify-PARSEDV-trav-controls-lua-1, page https://lanmower.github.io/oscraft/js/client/play.html at 1280x720): the lobby joins a room but stays at "loading world assets: still pending after 15 s"; console shows WebSocket wss://relay.damus.io/ handshake 503. A match cannot start, so the in-game witness is blocked by lobby-disabled-when-one-relay-503. CI 3292a7ca red on the existing workspace-tests row.

material.description: hy3d found that place-oscraft wrote the six pillar models (pillar-rock-1..6-skinned) but did not add their kinds to doodads.json, so the 41 pillar doodad lines would resolve to nothing. hy3d added the six keys by hand. place-oscraft adds entries for other props, so a new batch will hit the same gap. Locate why it skips these kinds and fix the tool.

Live oscraft doodads.json untouched. hy3d publish 1c5cb2a9; hy3d has no ci-status route.

material.description: Commit 41fdd376a names doodad codes from public tables and keeps their kinds, marking the reason UNVERIFIED. The project rule is that a value 6.88g does not give must not be filled from another source. A kind named from a public table is that kind of fill, so it should be withheld the way YTpb's kind is withheld, with its placements shown as they were or dropped with a note. Located in scenarios/moba/doodad-types-w3.tsv and scenarios/moba/tools/doodad-roles.mjs.

material.acceptance_criteria: A 1 px vertical drag moves the ground under the pointer by 1 px (within 1 percent) at pitch 0.3, 0.9 and 1.2, as horizontal drag already does; keyboard W/S pan speed matches A/D on screen.
material.commit_comment: Resolved on node witness; CI green at 0d8c127a
material.description: Fact: panCamera (js/client/render3d.js:210-218) scales every axis by k (render3d.js:211) and adds the forward vector times dyPx*k (render3d.js:215). The ground is seen foreshortened by sin(pitch), so 1 px of vertical drag moves the ground under the pointer by sin(pitch) px, not 1 px. Live evaluation of render3d.js (createCamera, panCamera, viewProjection, 1 px vertical drag, distance 30): 0.296 px at pitch 0.3, 0.784 px at pitch 0.9, 0.933 px at pitch 1.2. Horizontal drag tracks 1:1. Callers: js/client/play.js:1228 (renderer3d.pan on pointer drag), js/client/play.js:1097 (keyboard pan, vertical axis), js/client/editor.js:301 (middle or shift drag), render3d.js:556 (pan method). The comment at render3d.js:208-209 claims the scale is world units per pixel at the target; that holds only on the horizontal axis. Distinct from the devicePixelRatio scale in milner-trav-minimap-camera-1. Witness: codesearch dispatch 1792858394248-4308-646edc8c279bb72a (panCamera callers); no test under js/ references panCamera.

notes.note: Triage keep. Located: render3d.js:210-218 panCamera scales both axes by k (:211) and moves along the horizontal forward vector (:215); the comment at :208-209 says world units per pixel. A vertical pixel moves the ground under the pointer by sin(pitch) px, because the ground foreshortens. Observable: vertical drag (play.js:1228) and W/S keys (play.js:1097) lag the pointer at low pitch, about 30% at pitch 0.3. Reads: render3d.js 1-230 dispatch 1792859429069-6387-bfc94482968edb06; play.js 1095-1105 dispatch 1792859546359-6440-94a9f3ded5dfe3e5.

material.acceptance_criteria: gm.wait({ms:N}) replies only after about N ms have elapsed, and waited_ms equals the measured elapsed time.
material.description: gm.wait({ms:600000}) answered completed:true with waited_ms:600000 about 17 s after the previous dispatch. The icons directory holds 110 skinned hero PNGs and none of these 15 under any name. Where the 404 is requested: scenarios/moba/panels.lua:103 and :119 (hero_icon), js/client/play.js:2794, scenarios/moba/assets/assets.json:7177 (the icon entries for these heroes), scenarios/moba/assets/doodads.json:1013, scripts/npc or gen-heroes.mjs:194 (the generated name map), units_heroes.osd:26. The 6.88g rows for these heroes are present; only the icon file is missing. Fix in this row: (1) the client must not request an icon that is not on disk, so the lobby draws a text tile (hero name) for a hero whose icon is missing, with no 404; (2) keep the icon path in data only where the file exists, or mark the missing ones in assets.json so the list matches the disk; (3) do not download a pack and do not generate icons here. Acceptance: the census re-run on the live page after the change shows zero 404 for hero icons; CI green on the pushed sha. The 15 real icons are a user input and stay listed in the row body.

material.description: Evidence: scenarios/moba/assets/icons/heroes has 167 PNGs, 5,606,111 bytes in total, largest 82,087 bytes, all 256x256 RGBA from hy3d (copied in as 57 new files). scripts/assets/prep-icons.mjs shrinks icons to the page's draw size (128 px); its manifest scripts/assets/prep-manifest-icons.json lists only the 110 earlier icons, so the 57 new ones were never prepared. The first-draw gate (pages workflow, ceiling 10000 ms) failed on 3d5c3fe5 at a median of 10852 ms (run 40175451538), after the same tree measured 5835 ms earlier and 9352 ms on a rerun. Concurrent big downloads slow the wasm first draw (AGENTS: wasm is the bottleneck). Fix: run prep-icons on the hero icons (the script skips files the manifest already lists), commit the shrunk PNGs and the manifest, publish, and re-run the Pages gate. Acceptance: the icon bytes drop to about 40% of today; the pages first-draw job passes on the pushed sha. Do not change the 10000 ms ceiling; that is the owner's call.

Bytes heroes PNG 5,606,111 -> 2,881,370 (-48.6%), 167 files, names unchanged.

row.description: Evidence: scenarios/moba/assets/icons/heroes has 167 PNGs, 5,606,111 bytes in total, largest 82,087 bytes, all 256x256 RGBA from hy3d (copied in as 57 new files). scripts/assets/prep-icons.mjs shrinks icons to the page's draw size (128 px); its manifest scripts/assets/prep-manifest-icons.json lists only the 110 earlier icons, so the 57 new ones were never prepared. The first-draw gate (pages workflow, ceiling 10000 ms) failed on 3d5c3fe5 at a median of 10852 ms (run 40175451538), after the same tree measured 5835 ms earlier and 9352 ms on a rerun. Concurrent big downloads slow the wasm first draw (AGENTS: wasm is the bottleneck). Fix: run prep-icons on the hero icons (the script skips files the manifest already lists), commit the shrunk PNGs and the manifest, publish, and re-run the Pages gate. Acceptance: the icon bytes drop to about 40% of today; the pages first-draw job passes on the pushed sha. Do not change the 10000 ms ceiling; that is the owner's call.

material.description: Design, from the user: character icons carry their well-known acronym in capitals behind the icon, and the name under the icon goes. Contract for both lanes: a portraits item gains an optional string field badge. When badge is set, draw it in capitals, large and low-contrast, centred behind the icon (the portrait PNGs are RGBA, so the transparent areas show it; the icon draws on top). When text is empty or absent, draw no label under the icon. Items without badge render exactly as before. Ownership: js/client/widgets.js only. Acceptance: CI static client checks green on the pushed sha. Witness: the lobby screenshot after the panel lane lands.

material.description: Design, from the user: every character name has a well-known acronym; show it in capitals behind the icon and drop the name under the icon. Rule (default, for the user to review): a multi-word name gives its word initials (Anti-Mage -> AM, Sand King -> SK, Queen of Pain -> QOP, Nature's Prophet -> NP, Crystal Maiden -> CM); a one-word name gives its first three letters (Axe -> AXE, Lina -> LIN); hyphens split words, apostrophes are dropped. Overrides: a heroAcronyms object in scenarios/moba/moba_ui.json maps a hero name to its acronym, and wins over the rule. The grid tile passes badge = the acronym and text = "" to the portraits item (widget contract in row portraits-badge-behind-icon: badge and text fields). The right hero card and the seat strip keep the name. Ownership: scenarios/moba/panels.lua and scenarios/moba/moba_ui.json. Depends on portraits-badge-behind-icon for the badge field; the lane may land first if the field name matches the contract. Acceptance: the grid tiles show the acronym and no name under the icon; CI green on the pushed sha.

material.acceptance_criteria: At devicePixelRatio 1 and 2 a 100 CSS px drag moves the target the same world distance; panCamera receives the CSS viewport height, or pan converts deltas to device px.
material.description: play.js:1227-1228 takes dx/dy from clientX/clientY (CSS px) and calls renderer3d.pan. render3d.js:556 pan() passes gl.drawingBufferHeight as viewportHeightPx, and panCamera (render3d.js:211) divides the visible height by it. The canvas backing store is innerHeight*devicePixelRatio (play.js:1101-1103), so at DPR 2 the ground moves half the pointer distance. Keyboard pan (play.js:1097) uses the same path.

notes.note: Triage keep. Located: play.js:1227-1228 passes CSS-px dx,dy to renderer3d.pan; render3d.js:556 passes gl.drawingBufferHeight; panCamera (render3d.js:210-211) divides by it; play.js:1102-1103 sets the backing store to innerHeight*devicePixelRatio. Observable: at DPR 2 a 100 CSS px drag moves the ground half as far as the pointer. material.acceptance_criteria: After a minimap press on a blocked edge cell, a camera move, or setCamera, cam.target is inside cam.bounds. A property test over random press and move targets on a map with blocked edges asserts it.
material.description: PBTAGENT property: after every camera write, cam.target lies inside cam.bounds (the walkable box). Pan keeps it: panCamera ends in clampTarget (js/client/render3d.js:211-217; clampTarget 201-205). Three writes do not: setCamera sets target with no clamp (render3d.js:547-555); the camera move builds its target from ev.x/ev.y unclamped (js/client/modui.js:152-157) and writes it through setCamera (modui.js:166-176). The minimap maps any press across the full map extent (js/client/ui_minimap.js:175-182, centre(fx*mapSize.w, fz*mapSize.h)), sent as camera_to (js/client/hud.js:71; scenarios/moba/controls.lua:561 passes fx(args.x) through unclamped; the sim-side game.camera clamp is not verified in this lane). cameraBounds is the walkable extent (js/client/play.js:478-479, from walkableBounds at js/client/tiles.js:109-121), smaller than the map whenever edge cells are blocked or cliff. Symptom: a press on the minimap's blocked border leaves the view centred outside the walkable box, and the next drag snaps the target back (render3d.js:217). Witness: fs_read dispatches 1792859120895-6134-cc2f7e9573f9e487 (modui.js 150-158), 1792859124044-6136-9bf589406449a7dc (play.js 470-483), 1792859130215-6145-aae895c3e6f866d7 (tiles.js 105-125), 1792858779532-5837-15898496847076db (render3d.js 540-560, setCamera), 1792858675059-5723-87361a00d6f186f4 (ui_minimap.js whole file).

notes.note: Triage keep. Located: setCamera render3d.js:547-553 writes target with no clampTarget; modui.js:156-157 builds the camera-event target from ev.x/ev.y unclamped and step (modui.js:174-177) writes it through setCamera. panCamera clamps via clampTarget (render3d.js:201-205, :210-218) against cam.bounds, which play.js:2741 sets to cameraBounds (play.js:479; walkableBounds tiles.js:109-121 excludes blocked and cliff cells). material.description: Found while resolving gm-friction-minimap-witness-drain-gui-minimap-1 (item 3). The localhost witnesses ran stale code: the server answered ui_minimap.js at 7079 bytes, the pre-edit size, while the working tree held the edit. The server serves .dev-site, which stage.sh lays out (docs/QUICKSTART.md, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:17 'Serves .dev-site on http://localhost:8790'), so the served file is a staged copy that the working tree edit never reaches until it is staged again. Witnesses went through raw.githubusercontent at the pushed sha instead.

material.description: Blocking fact for content-tree-layer-not-converged: the 2,392 w3 tree records (ATtr 1141, NTtw 756, CTtr 495, sum checked in scenarios/moba/doodad-types-w3.tsv) have no 54-byte doodads.bin on disk, so convert-688g-map.mjs (DOO_RECORD = 54, reads doodads.bin from its --src extract) cannot convert the tree layer. Searched in this run: codesearch filename 'adapter' under the hy3d root returns only tools/bpy-venv requests/adapters.py; codesearch literal '54-byte' under hy3d returns 0 matches in the 2036 scanned files; a walk of hy3d for doodad*.bin returns none; hy3d/output/map-diff holds only TSV and OSD forms (doodads-w3.tsv, doodad-types-w3.tsv, doodads-w3-placed.tsv, map-w3.osd, map-w3-full.osd). The oscraft tree has no gen-w3-map.mjs although the placer header and map.osd comment still name it. Witness now: map.osd tree lines 3479, mapped 1330 at HEAD 828edc06. Clearing action: run the hy3d adapter in its owning checkout to emit doodads.bin for the w3 target (16-byte header, 54-byte records for the 2392 tree records, 8-byte special block) into an --src dir, then run convert-688g-map.mjs --src <dir> and witness the tree count in map.osd. Do not regenerate pathability by hand.

material.description: Owner decision (user, session drain-ci-policy-12): maximise parity and CI speed; tests are not what we value. Every test job moves out of push CI into .github/workflows/tests.yml, which runs on workflow_dispatch only: the rust workspace tests, the wasm32 and wasip3 compile, the native and wasm state-hash parity, the map export determinism check and the wire codec round-trip. Test source files stay in git and are not deleted. Push CI (ci.yml) keeps the static client checks and gains the browser smoke of the built page. pages.yml keeps the build, the static gate, the deploy and the first-draw gate; its wire gate moves to tests.yml.

material.body: Audit (read-only): unit_rules.lua:68-79 calls six set_* natives per unit per tick; targeting.lua:129-141 re-picks targets and calls cmd_strike every tick; panels.lua:756-768 rebuilds all trees every 4 ticks before the diff; upgrades.lua:42-57 scans held items every tick; heroes.lua:224-234 runs attribute_bonuses every tick. Fix: change-gated setters, target re-pick on change or interval, dirty flags per panel. Witness: a per-tick cost measurement before and after; the 75-test suite must stay green. Re-audit (drain-f-1): setter gating already present (unit_rules.lua:72-102, heroes.lua:138-149); the item scan, panel rebuild and targeting re-pick have no host change signal, so the row is blocked_by perf-lua-per-tick-setters-blocker-drain-f-1. Current witness is 24 ok lines and 53 passed.
material.commit_comment: Lua per-tick target scan replaced by strike_reach native; 4.16 -> 2.70 ms per tick (-35%), hashes identical, published 3a09b208

notes.note: Gated: upgrades.lua on_tick via game.unit_item_gen (seen cache); panels.lua inventory tree via inventory_tree_cached (emit_all). Published 58f7c010d4287a3e2c094aed4d1e0acf5a4385d1, all CI check runs success. NOT gated, blocking facts: (1) targeting.lua on_tick 177-187 re-picks each tick through strike_choice (165-170 reads unit_position, range and best_in_reach); positions move every tick, so a target-set generation would freeze the pick and change strikes. (2) panels.lua hud_tree 225-237 reads hp, gold and clock (clock_text 214-222, game.time); skills_tree 452-460 reads remaining cooldowns; emit (136-146) dedups the output but the rebuild still runs. Gating those needs tick-varying inputs in the signal, an owner decision.
drain-controls-shard-2: scan lane left pending by default. Blocker unchanged: targeting re-pick (targeting.lua on_tick) cannot be change-gated without changing strike behaviour; no edit made.

survey-sim-8 evidence: scenarios/moba/targeting.lua:31 calls config.rule("aggro_priority") for every candidate of every unit in best_in_reach via target_class_order (line 144), so a string-keyed rule read runs units x candidates per tick; targeting.lua:178-187 sets cmd_strike for every living unit every tick; scenarios/moba/upgrades.lua:46-48 walks game.units() and reads unit_item_gen per unit per tick. Hoist the rule read to once per tick.
drain-ui-panels-9: left open; targeting.lua re-pick (177-187) cannot be change-gated without altering strike behaviour, no code route in my files.
claimed by drain-rust-10

drain-rust-10: no mod-host route with gain. cmd_strike (piccolo_host.rs:1430) only pushes Cmd::SetStrike; skipping unchanged would save a Vec push while the cost is the Lua strike_choice scan and per-unit native calls, which also move the applied counter. Gating targeting.lua on_tick is a pack change that alters strike behaviour; left open.
Owner decision (user): anything may change to remove this cost; pick the best choice (batched or skipped setters, see perf-setters lane).

Measured (local parity_hash, moba pack, one data snapshot, CPU seconds, same binary): before 4800 ticks 20.11 s = 4.16 ms per tick; after 13.10 s = 2.70 ms per tick (-35%). State hashes identical at 0, 1200 and 4800 ticks (4800: 321bdcd02a0cb622). Earlier ablations on an older snapshot: the targeting on_tick cost 1.37 ms per tick (doubling it), now about 0.49 ms; unit_rules on_tick about 1.04 ms per tick before its arithmetic rewrite, the rewrite saved about 0.5 ms. Shipped: game.strike_reach native (rust/crates/mod-host/src/piccolo_host.rs:1250) replaces the per-tick Lua grid and candidate scan (scenarios/moba/targeting.lua strike_choice:136); unit_rules.lua same formulas without math natives. Not done: per-unit cmd_strike skip (unsafe: arrays.rs resets strike_target on slot init). Remaining per-tick hooks not re-measured: upgrades.lua scan, heroes.lua attribute_bonuses, panels.lua rebuild every 4 ticks.

material.acceptance_criteria: Either the queue is held in sim state and survives a keyframe resync, or a resynced peer restores the queue; a two-client resync during a shift-queued move leaves both clients issuing the same orders.
material.description: UNVERIFIED LEAD from trav-controls-lua. The shift-queue that controls.lua builds (around line 218) is kept in the Lua mod, not in the sim. A peer that resyncs from a keyframe during a shift-queue would not have the queued orders, so its queue would differ from the one the player sees. Not reproduced yet; the lane marked it as a lead, not a finding.

notes.note: Not reproduced, not fixed. Reproduction needs two live clients in a match (a keyframe resync mid-shift-queue). Live check (browser dispatch 1792862772886-5303-5a481f4722e0f263, session verify-PARSEDV-trav-controls-lua-1, page https://lanmower.github.io/oscraft/js/client/play.html at 1280x720): the lobby joins a room but stays at "loading world assets: still pending after 15 s"; console shows WebSocket wss://relay.damus.io/ handshake 503. A match cannot start, so the in-game witness is blocked by lobby-disabled-when-one-relay-503. Left pending.

drain-controls-shard-2: not reproduced, left pending. The shift queue is controls.lua QUEUE (pack Lua state), and the page exposes no queue state; the only observable is unit positions via oscraft.getState. A two-client keyframe-resync check was not run: the premise that a resynced guest diverges is unverified.

Not driven this run. Live witness blocked: gm browser verb claims the dispatch and never writes its out-file (5 tries, gm-mcp 0.2.302 and 0.2.305, bodies with and without gm_session_id, about:blank included); each holds the state lane until the 600 s watchdog. Clearing action: fix the browser executor in the agentplug runner.
survey-sim-8: same class as new row lua-module-caches-survive-load-state-swap (effects, targeting, upgrades caches also survive load_state/swap_data); a shared reset hook would cover QUEUE too.
drain-ui-panels-9: needs two live clients (browser) to reproduce resync mid-shift-queue; left open.
claimed by drain-rust-10

drain-rust-10 plan (not implemented, not contained): QUEUE (scenarios/moba/controls.lua:218) is Lua-module state and is not in sim save/hash. Fix needs (1) a per-unit order queue in sim (rust/crates/sim, persisted in persist.rs and hashed, so a save-format and hash change for every scenario), (2) natives game.queue_order/queue_clear/queue_pop in mod-host, (3) controls.lua :248-270 and :595-612 moved onto them. Interim shipped by drain-rust-10: host now runs on_state_replaced(state) in every module after load_state/set_sim, so a module can drop or rebuild its queue on resync; controls.lua does not yet use it.
Owner decision (user): choose the most efficient solution; a sim-side queue is accepted, including a save format and hash change. Keep determinism for everything else.

Sim-side order queue commit: 2fe55295c80dd31af3759e64ef28f887fc43adf6 (Row: controls-queued-orders-outside-sim-state, STATE_VERSION 43->44). CI on 2fe55295c: ci run 40184805513 has 1 failing job (built page smoke, console 404, fixed upstream by a090c61d, a CI smoke fix from another lane, which exempts /__hmr); pages 4/4 success. Origin main is 3a09b2080dad6b44eb7ccdafe603daacf2d456a1 (contains 2fe55295c). Not closed: close needs a green ci on the witnessed sha; closing on a090c61d is refused by the owner.

material.description: User report: after Fill with bots and Start match, the GUI (the Hero select modal) is not removed. Path: scenarios/moba/panels.lua lobby_act start (around line 726-730) sets L.started and emits lobby_started_event; ui_call skips lobby_seats_event for start; the next refresh (game.timer panels, REFRESH_TICKS) calls emit_all, which emits the lobby modal as lobby_tree() = nil, so emit() should send a widget remove. material.description: After the closing push 53eecaea (10:48:56Z), two tests runs (40186321689 at 10:49:05Z and 40186341621 at 10:49:23Z, both event workflow_dispatch) ran on that sha, 5 jobs each. drain-ci-policy-12 did not dispatch them; the source is not identified. A tests run after every push defeats the CI-speed decision (ci-tests-on-demand-speed-decision): push runs would carry the test cost again. Find the caller (a gm-mcp push hook, a sibling lane, or a scheduled dispatch) and stop it; tests run only when an operator dispatches them.

material.commit_comment: Guard already shipped; witnessed pass-on-tip and fail-on-4-letter-override.
material.description: From the user (twice): no acronym longer than 3 letters. The cap is in acronym() and the precomputed table in scenarios/moba/panels.lua plus heroAcronyms overrides in moba_ui.json, verified by reading only. Add scripts/check-acronyms.mjs (a check script like scripts/check-fx.mjs, not a test file) that reads the roster names, the table and the overrides, computes each hero's acronym the way the Lua does (override first), and fails when any is empty, longer than 3 letters, not A-Z, or duplicated; print the offenders. Wire it into the static client checks job in .github/workflows/ci.yml next to check-fx.mjs. Acceptance: the check passes on the current tip and fails when a 4-letter override is added (prove it once, locally by reading the script logic is not enough: run it with node on a temp copy). CI green on ci and pages. Ownership: scripts/check-acronyms.mjs and .github/workflows/ci.yml. No public references: the guard is a project-local roster/table consistency check with no upstream implementation to derive from.

material.commit_comment: Table and fallback-free acronym() already shipped; witnessed by the generator output and both checkers.
material.description: From the user: scrolling down the lobby grid shows many acronyms longer than 3 letters. Cause: scenarios/moba/panels.lua acronym(name) returns UI.heroAcronyms[name] or HERO_ACRONYM_RULE[name] or name; HERO_ACRONYM_RULE holds 69 names but the roster (player-controlled kinds in units_heroes.osd and units.osd) is larger, and the mod VM has no string library to shorten a name at run time, so the fallback shows the full name. Fix: (1) scenarios/moba/tools/gen-hero-acronyms.mjs reads every roster hero name and writes scenarios/moba/hero_acronyms.lua (a table name -> acronym), rule: word initials (hyphens split, apostrophes dropped); if more than 3, drop the stop words of and the, then truncate to 3; one-word names keep their first 3 letters; heroAcronyms overrides in moba_ui.json win; collisions are resolved deterministically (the later name gets a distinct 3-letter form, e.g. first letter of the first word plus first two letters of the second) and listed in the commit body for the user to review; (2) panels.lua requires hero_acronyms.lua (and scenarios/moba/manifest.json modules lists it: check-fx.mjs fails otherwise; remember the pack-load test only follows a literal require) and acronym() has no fallback to the full name (an unknown name returns its first 3 letters via a precomputed table or a short marker, never the full name); (3) scripts/check-acronyms.mjs (row hero-acronym-ci-guard-max-three-letters, in flight) also fails when a roster hero has no entry. Acceptance: every roster hero has a unique acronym of 1 to 3 letters, ci and pages green (watch for a Lua error: main has gone red from panels.lua before); screenshot after deploy shows no tile with a long label while scrolling. Ownership: scenarios/moba/panels.lua, hero_acronyms.lua (new), tools/gen-hero-acronyms.mjs (new), moba_ui.json heroAcronyms, manifest.json modules. No public references: the acronym table is generated from this repository roster only, so no upstream implementation applies.
material.subject: Acronym table covers 69 heroes; any other roster hero shows its full name (acronym() falls back to name)
material.witness: panels.lua:1213 acronym() returns UI.heroAcronyms[name] or HERO_ACRONYM[name] or "?", no full-name fallback; hero_acronyms.lua has 127 entries, 0 outside 1-3 A-Z, 0 duplicates; manifest.json lists hero_acronyms.lua; check-modules PASS (92 modules), check-acronyms PASS (127 heroes).

material.acceptance_criteria: Each narrowing is checked (try_from with a named bail) or validate.rs refuses the over-long value before encode runs; mapexport on an oversized name exits with a message.
material.description: rust/crates/data/src/format.rs:204 name.len() as u8 in encode_name_list; rust/crates/data/src/encode.rs:19 text.len() as u16 in Strings.intern, :263 route.points.len() as u16. validate.rs bounds some counts (:127,:220,:302) but not name byte length or route points; a 256-byte name or 65536-byte string would wrap and write a corrupt image that reader.rs may still accept. No public references: the OSDT image layout is this repository's own, so no upstream implementation applies. Name-list entries and route points are already refused upstream (validate.rs bounds each name list entry to one byte; the OSDT parser refuses route points past 64), leaving the string table as the last unchecked narrowing.
